summary: An interview with compliance expert Elizabeth Harmon (conducted October 15, 2023) on the regulatory and compliance difficulties facing small businesses. She describes a five-stage compliance lifecycle, the financial burden of compliance, the role of software, and the value of a compliance-friendly culture and dedicated staff. She advises vigilance, using grants and local support programs, and building ties with the business community.
one_line: Compliance expert Elizabeth Harmon explains how small businesses can manage complex, changing regulations through a compliance lifecycle, technology, culture, and community support.
key_facts: Elizabeth Harmon is a compliance expert with over 20 years of experience, interviewed on October 15, 2023.
Small business owners voiced concerns about increasing regulatory complexity after September 1, 2023.
Harmon says requirements differ by industry, location, business size, and products or services offered; a restaurant faces different health and safety rules than a construction business.
Harmon warned, "Ignorance of the law is not a defense," with consequences ranging from fines to closure of the business.
Harmon's "compliance lifecycle" has five stages: Awareness, Implementation, Monitoring, Reporting, and Improvement.
Since November 2023, there has been a surge in environmental regulations affecting local businesses, according to Harmon.
A common monitoring pitfall is thinking compliance is finished once achieved, though regulatory bodies update rules regularly.
Slips in record keeping and reporting can lead to penalties or audits.
Financial pressures from compliance contributed to the closure of several small businesses in the last quarter of 2023.
Harmon suggests government grants or local support programs to help offset compliance-related expenses.
Compliance software has an upfront cost but can streamline processes, reduce human error, automatically update regulatory changes, ease reporting, and maintain documentation for audits.
Harmon says "Compliance should be everyone's responsibility" and recommends integrating it into the business model and educating employees.
She recommends a designated person or team to handle compliance, since automated systems lack nuance and flexibility.
Harmon recommends joining chambers of commerce or industry associations for information and support.
